classes.name: Привремено народно представништво Краљевства Срба, Хрвата и Словенаца
classes.locator: https://www.parlament.gov.rs/народна-скупштина/историјат/историјат-1804---1918.117.html ("Српска народна скупштина састала се последњи пут 14. децембра 1918. године. На основу саопштења Краљевске владе, изабрала је из својих редова 84 посланика за Привремено народно представништво Краљевства СХС")
classes.note: A body delegated, not elected, by the existing representative bodies of the uniting lands (the Serbian National Assembly chose 84 of its members on 14 December 1918, and the National Council in Zagreb, the Montenegrin and Vojvodina assemblies, and the provincial diets sent their own); it first met on 1 March 1919 and sat until the Constituent Assembly was elected.

dates.quote: Српска народна скупштина састала се последњи пут 14. децембра 1918. године. На основу саопштења Краљевске владе, изабрала је из својих редова 84 посланика за Привремено народно представништво Краљевства СХС.
dates.note: The Serbian National Assembly's delegation; the other lands' delegations followed until the body first met on 1 March 1919 (Archives of Yugoslavia: "Привремено народно представништво састало се 1. марта 1919").

classes.disposition_reason: Delegations named by the uniting lands' bodies; the composition is recorded only in the printed proceedings of the Provisional National Representation, of which no official digital copy was found.

classes.name: Избори за Уставотворну скупштину (1920 и 1945)
classes.finest_note: 1920: by electoral district and county in the Constituent Assembly's printed statistics; 1945: by federal unit and constituency in the printed records of the Assembly.
classes.note: The Constituent Assembly of the Kingdom, elected on 28 November 1920 by universal male suffrage with list PR in the electoral districts, adopted the Vidovdan Constitution on 28 June 1921 and continued as the National Assembly. The Constituent Assembly of Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, elected on 11 November 1945 with two chambers (the Federal Assembly by population and the Assembly of Nations by federal unit) on single People's Front lists with a "box without a list", proclaimed the Federal People's Republic on 29 November 1945 and adopted the Constitution of 31 January 1946.

dates.quote: Округи су остали исти који су били и приликом избора за Уставотворну Скупштину; једино је од Северне Далмације, која је у време избора за Конституанту била окупирана од италијанских трупа, образован нов изборни округ Шибеник и област Задарског Суда.
dates.note: 55 districts: the 56 of 1923 less Šibenik, which the cited page says was formed after 1920. Day and the 419 seats are not quoted from a fetched source; the Constituent Assembly's own statistics were not found online.

dates.quote: Уставотворна скупштина је на првој заједничкој седници оба дома (Савезна скупштина и Скупштина народа) ...
dates.note: Two chambers: the Federal Assembly and the Assembly of Nations. Day not quoted from a fetched source; constituency and seat counts are not yet listed.

classes.disposition_reason: The Constituent Assembly's 1920 statistics and the 1945 returns survive only in print; no official digital copy was found.

classes.name: Избори за народне посланике Народне скупштине Краљевине СХС / Југославије
classes.finest_note: The National Assembly's statistics give votes by electoral district (okrug) and electoral county (srez); 1931-1938 the national list's votes by district and county.
classes.note: Unicameral under the Vidovdan Constitution of 28 June 1921, with list PR in electoral districts and candidates by county (1923, 1925, 1927). The law of 6 January 1929 dissolved it; under the Constitution of 3 September 1931 it became the lower chamber of the National Representation, elected on a national list that had to carry candidates in every county, with open public voting (1931, 1935, 1938). Deputies elected on 11 December 1938 sat until the April 1941 invasion.

access.platform: Дигитална библиотека Управе за заједничке послове републичких органа
access.evidence: The 1923 statistics, issued by the National Assembly in 1924, downloaded whole (207 pages); the library lists no statistics for the other elections.

dates.quote: У I. табели означено је да наша Држава бира 312 посланика. Она у ствари бира 313 посланика, само приликом последњих избора један посланик није могао да буде изабран у крајевима Северне Далмације
dates.note: 56 electoral districts (p. VI, § 7).

classes.name: Избори сенатора (1932-1941)
classes.name_en: Senate of the Kingdom (indirectly elected half, 1932-1941)
classes.locator: https://www.arhivyu.rs/leksikon-jugoslavije/konstitutivni_akti_jugoslavije (Октроисани устав, 3. септембар 1931: "Уведено је дводомно Народно представништво састављено од Сената и Народне скупштине. Краљ је имао право да именује онолико сенатора колико их је бирано на посредним изборима.")
classes.note: Half the senators were elected indirectly in each banovina by an electoral body of the banovina's deputies, councillors, and municipal heads, and the King appointed as many again; half the elected senators were renewed every three years.

dates.note: First Senate election. Day not quoted from a fetched source.
Triennial renewals of half the elected senators; not yet dated from the Senate's records.

classes.disposition_reason: Votes of the banovina electoral bodies are recorded only in the printed Senate proceedings and the Službene novine; no official digital copy was found.

classes.name: Избори за обласне скупштине
classes.note: The Vidovdan Constitution gave each of the 33 oblasts an elected oblast assembly (Archives of Yugoslavia: "Органи обласне управе били су обласна скупштина и обласни одбор"). The only election was held on 23 January 1927; the law of 6 January 1929 suspended oblast self-government and the banovinas replaced the oblasts on 3 October 1929.

dates.note: One assembly in each of the 33 oblasts. Day not quoted from a fetched source.

classes.disposition_reason: Results were published by the oblasts and in the Službene novine; no official digital copy was found.

classes.name: Општински избори у Краљевини СХС / Југославији
classes.note: Municipal councils were elected under the provincial laws inherited in 1918 until the Law on Municipalities of 1933 unified them; elections under that law were held banovina by banovina from 1933 to 1936. The law of 6 January 1929 dissolved the elected municipal administrations of Belgrade, Zagreb, and Ljubljana.

dates.note: Municipal elections across the Kingdom; not yet dated from the banovinas' gazettes.

classes.disposition_reason: Returns were published, if at all, in the provincial and banovina gazettes; no official digital copy was found.

dates.note: Federal Council and Council of Nationalities. Day not quoted from a fetched source.

dates.quote: The 3 Councils of Working Communities — Economic Council, Educational and Cultural Council and Council for Social Affairs and Health — each have 120 members designated by electoral colleges composed of the councillors of the communal assemblies and delegates from the working communities.

The Council of Nationalities ... has 140 members elected by the republican and provincial assemblies at a joint sitting of all their councils — 20 members for each Republic and 10 for each of the 2 Autonomous Provinces.

classes.name_en: Assembly of the SFRY under the delegate system (1974-1986)
classes.note: Under the 1974 Constitution the 220 delegates of the Federal Chamber (30 per republic and 20 per province) were elected by the communal assemblies from lists drawn up by the Socialist Alliance, and the 88 of the Chamber of Republics and Provinces (12 per republic and 8 per province) by the republican and provincial assemblies, for four years. No federal election was held in 1990; the delegates of 1986 sat until the federation dissolved.

classes.name_en: President of the Republic and members of the Presidency (chosen by assemblies, 1953-1991)
classes.note: The Federal People's Assembly elected the President of the Republic from 1953 (the 1963 Constitution set a four-year term with no limit for Josip Broz Tito). From 1971 the collective Presidency's members were elected by the republican and provincial assemblies, and from 1974 Tito held the presidency without term. The direct popular votes for Slovenia's member of the Presidency in 1989 were run by the republic and belong to its census.

dates.note: Elections of the President by the Federal Assembly and of the Presidency's members by the republican and provincial assemblies; not yet dated.

classes.name: Избори за савезне посланике у Веће грађана Савезне скупштине СРЈ
classes.name_en: Chamber of Citizens of the Federal Assembly (1992-2000)
classes.finest_note: The Federal Statistical Office published results by constituency and polling station for 1996 and by constituency and municipality for 2000; for May 1992 the Serbian statistical office published Serbia's results by constituency.
classes.note: 138 deputies (108 from Serbia and 30 from Montenegro) for four years. May 1992: half of Serbia's seats in 54 single-member constituencies and half by list in Serbia as one constituency, and in Montenegro 6 by constituency and 24 by list. From December 1992 list PR in multi-member constituencies with the D'Hondt method: 36 in 1996 (7 in Montenegro and 29 in Serbia), and in 2000 Montenegro as one constituency and 26 in Serbia. The Federal Electoral Commission declared the results.

access.evidence: The Federal Statistical Office's volumes for 1996 (G19966001) and 2000 (G20006001) and the Serbian office's May 1992 volume (G19926001) downloaded whole; the December 1992 federal volume was not identified.

dates.quote: вишестраначки избори су, у Републици Србији и Републици Црној Гори као републикама чланицама, одржани 31. маја 1992. године. У Републици Србији бирано је укупно 108 посланика у Веће грађана
dates.note: Serbia: 54 single-member constituencies and one list constituency; Montenegro: 6 single-member seats and 24 list seats (IPU).

dates.quote: Dates of elections / renewal (from/to): 20 December 1992 3 January 1993
dates.note: Early election after the constitutional amendments of September 1992; repeat voting on 3 January 1993. Constituency count not yet listed.

dates.quote: Савезна република Југославија је подељена на 36 изборних јединица, па се у Црној Гори бира 30 посланика у 7 изборних јединица а у Србији 108 посланика у 29 изборних јединица.

У овој публикацији Савезни завод за статистику објављује резултате избора за савезне посланике у Већу република и Већу грађана Савезне скупштине Савезне Републике Југославије, који су одржани 24. септембра 2000. године у СР Југославији.

classes.name: Савезни референдум
classes.note: No referendum was held across Yugoslavia: the monarchy was abolished by the Constituent Assembly's declaration of 29 November 1945, and the referendums of 1990-1992 on independence, sovereignty, and state symbols were each called and run by one republic.
classes.disposition_reason: No federal referendum was ever held; the republican referendums belong to the successor states' censuses.
